A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same WIND study with complete, readable main text and Appendices A-I. All pages except the first-page version stamp and Figure 5 page render identically, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original watermark detection, attack robustness, image-quality, and runtime results in Section 5 and Appendices D and G.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical evaluations, including detection accuracies, image-quality measurements, attack experiments, and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1-2, seeded initial-noise generation, Fourier group identifiers, WIND fast/full detection, and the inpainting approach are unchanged.

E1.justification: The generated-image evaluations, COCO inpainting task, prompt source, and attack scenarios are unchanged. Figure 5 retains the same three prompts.

E2.justification: Tree-Ring and RingID remain in Figure 5 and Table 1. Comparator membership in the additional comparisons in Tables 3, 10, and 14 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain the same generation/inversion settings, key/group configurations, attack strengths, metrics, and appendix evaluation protocols. The replaced Figure 5 image does not establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: The iterative-regeneration analysis, inference-step sensitivity, additional attack tests, and image-quality analyses in Appendix D are unchanged. Figure 5 replaces an illustrative output within the existing comparison.

E5.justification: Means, standard deviations, and p-value statements retain the same reporting practices. Neither version adds or revises run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Figure 5's Tree-Ring 'Enchanted Village' panel changes: v4 duplicates the WIND image, whereas v5 displays a distinct village image. This revises one qualitative result entry; numerical results and stated findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, its cryptographic assumptions and Appendix E proof, and the distortion arguments in Section 3 and Appendix F are unchanged.

C1.justification: The claims about initial-noise watermarking, two-stage detection efficiency, robustness to attacks, and applicability through inpainting are unchanged in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendices C and F retain the same interpretations and limitations concerning distortion, runtime tradeoffs, private-model assumptions, and editing or forgery vulnerabilities.

D1.justification: Appendices G-H retain identical hardware, runtime setup, prompt source, detection thresholds, and retrieval details. The project-code link and its target are unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work discussions, including positioning relative to Tree-Ring and Gaussian Shading, are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the marginal arXiv version/date text changes from v4, 13 March 2025, to v5, 27 April 2025. Manuscript prose, terminology, captions, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 replaces the duplicated village panel, uses higher-resolution image assets, and slightly adjusts panel sizing, spacing, and heading placement. Other figures, tables, and page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 5 no longer presents the identical village image under both WIND and Tree-Ring, removing a confusing duplication in the qualitative comparison. This is a limited improvement to the displayed evidence; the quantitative results, methods, theory, and conclusions remain unchanged.
